Care by animal

Common concerns, sorted by species.

A quick starting point for owners of every kind of animal. It helps you pick the right kind of care, not diagnose.

Dogs

  • Limping or stiffness
  • Ear scratching and skin allergies
  • Vomiting or loose stools

Cats

  • Hiding or not eating
  • Litter-box changes
  • Sneezing and watery eyes

Birds & exotics

  • Fluffed feathers, low energy
  • Beak or feather problems
  • Diet and housing checks

Cows & buffalo

  • Reduced milk or appetite
  • Fever and bloating
  • Hoof and udder care

Goats & sheep

  • Worms and weight loss
  • Cough and nasal discharge
  • Vaccination schedules

Hens & poultry

  • Drop in egg laying
  • Respiratory signs in the flock
  • Biosecurity and vaccines
FAQ

Questions owners ask us most.

Can’t see yours? Tell us and we’ll add it.

How do I know if it’s an emergency?

Trouble breathing, collapse, heavy bleeding, seizures, a swollen belly or suspected poisoning need a vet right away. Use the Emergency shortcut and call ahead.

What does “verified” mean on a listing?

A verified badge means the provider’s details were checked by our team. Each provider’s profile shows what was confirmed.

Can I find care for farm animals?

Yes. Filter by cows, goats or poultry, or look for ambulance and large-animal services in the listing tags.

What should I bring to the first visit?

Past vaccination records, any medicines your pet takes, a stool or urine sample if asked, and a note of when symptoms began.

Are the ratings and hours accurate?

Hours and ratings are supplied by providers and reviewers. Please call ahead for urgent needs, and use “Submit a correction” if anything looks wrong.

Is this a substitute for a vet’s advice?

No. Pawfind helps you find and compare care. Only a qualified vet can diagnose or treat your animal.
